coordinates.note: This site is used as the placement for ProtoDUNE-SP, ProtoDUNE-DP and the ICARUS refurbishment, none of which has its own dedicated site record. `kind` is set to `detector` only because A17/the validator requires that for any site holding a detector placement; the coordinate itself is the OpenStreetMap/Nominatim point for CERN's whole Prevessin site, not a surveyed position for the EHN1 building (also known as Building 887, ~330 m long). Real effort (CERN's Neutrino Platform page, the North Area experimental-areas pages, and open-days material) confirmed the building's identity and general siting on the Prevessin site but did not turn up a published lat/lon for EHN1 itself. Treat every placement at this site as campus-precision, not building precision. CERN publishes no coordinate for the hall on the fetched page.
coordinates.quote: located in a test-beam hall on CERN’s Prévessin site

name: CERN Neutrino Platform, EHN1 (Prévessin site)
notes: facility:cern is owned by the cern-atlas workstream; this record only references it.

Coordinates are shown at campus (Prevessin-site) precision; see coordinates.note. `kind: detector` is a schema requirement (this site hosts several detector placements), not a claim of survey-grade precision for the EHN1 building.

summary.plain: A large hall at CERN, on the French side of the laboratory, where full-size prototypes of the DUNE detectors were built and tested in a particle beam.
summary.technical: EHN1 extension in the CERN North Area on the Prévessin site, housing the CERN Neutrino Platform test beams and the ProtoDUNE single-phase and dual-phase cryostats, as well as ICARUS refurbishment and Baby MIND.
